money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Cash declaration: the Turks and Caicos Islands Border Force requires a declaration for more than US$10,000 (or the equivalent) carried in or out, on a Report of International Transportation of Money form given to an officer. It covers notes, coins, bearer bonds, cheques, money orders and gold coins or bullion. US$10,000 is about A$14,205 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026 (A$1 = USD 0.7040). Undeclared cash can be seized and legal action taken.

laws.rule: Cannabis is a Class B drug. Possession: up to 3 years and/or USD 40,000 on summary conviction, or up to 7 years on indictment (s 6(2)). Possession with intent to supply: up to 15 years on indictment.

In Turks and Caicos national parks and other protected areas (national parks, nature reserves, sanctuaries and areas of historical interest), fishing is prohibited, with fines of USD 50,000 per offence as stated by the tourism authority. Camping, making fires and littering are also prohibited and carry fines. The Department of Environment and Coastal Resources (DECR) enforces this.
laws.penalty_signal: Fishing in a protected area: up to USD 50,000 per infraction (about A$71,023 at USD 0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026).

laws.rule: A traveller leaving the Turks and Caicos may take at most 3 Queen Conch shells in checked luggage. Other conch products, or more than 3 shells, need a CITES export permit (allow 3 to 5 working days). Under general policy there is no export of coral, live or dead, or of sea turtle products.
